rites.name: Sheizasha
rites.text: Sheizasha is a concept of the Singing in Crodaston, the sound that first gathered the roots of the world during the Age of Sundering. It is a standing note that holds the earth together when landfall breaks old bonds between shelves of stone.

rites.name: Oriallemwen
rites.text: Oriallemwen is the sounding-pitch that the first roots of Crodaston took when they condensed from the Singing, a thin hum that settled into stone and sap. During the Age of Strangers, outsiders learned to anchor their own songs to it and trade in the resonance it left behind.

rites.name: Ukavarraum
rites.text: Ukavarraum is a concept in the Crodaston universe, bound to the Courts of the Second Era, when councils judged divine trials and the doors between worlds were raised. It is remembered as the principle by which a sacred flame is kept lit within the temples of the Holy Age. Its presence is felt most in the orders that tend the fire and read its signs.

rites.name: Isesheth
rites.text: Isesheth is a concept in Crodaston, the idea of a bond that held together in the Fall and was tested by the Sundering. It came to mean the promise made among the Shards to keep what could still be kept. Its strength was in people's willingness to share the weight of what had broken.

rites.name: Telauranum
rites.text: A battle craft where striking vulnerable spots briefly sharpens a blade's force. Landing precise blows also empowers the wielder's deadliest strikes for a short span.

rites.name: Lianor
rites.text: A learned craft in which a wielder gathers trophies from fallen foes to strengthen their weapon handling. A refined version of the same practice deepens these gains.

rites.name: Teleolus
rites.text: A tactic that lets a fighter move low along the ground while wielding a ranged arm. An improved form of the same technique strengthens the fighter's capability.

rites.name: Ameonanum
rites.text: A learned talent that lets a fighter improve the gear they carry into battle. An upgraded form of this craft makes those improvements stronger.

rites.name: Telaureolus
rites.text: A quiet practice of sitting with a grieving person after a loss, offering presence and encouragement. It helps the bereaved avoid replaying painful moments and teaches them to rise above sorrow.

rites.name: Naustentium
rites.text: Each slain foe swells the bearer's striking force by a tenth, and this surge lasts only while the attacks continue. Such swelling can accumulate across as many as five slayings.

rites.name: Nenares
rites.text: A binding hold placed over a person, letting an overseer bring them in while keeping them under watch. The subject may or may not be told they have been seized.

rites.name: Liarantium
rites.text: A battle gift that lets a warrior who breaks an opponent's vulnerable spot refresh their own abilities and those of allies standing close by. It can trigger only once every short span of time.

rites.name: Veosilium
rites.text: A tactic of steady resolve that lets a marksman or gunner keep firing despite pressure. It can be applied to pistols, rifles, shotguns, and other handheld firearms.

rites.name: Amastium Orolia
rites.text: A learned knack for turning harm dealt in battle into a tradeable measure of worth. An improved form of the knack allows greater returns from each exchange.

rites.name: Kaluvaari
rites.text: Kaluvaari is a concept of Crodaston's Walled Age, a notion of the wall as a sworn promise kept by lamp-lit orders. It is said to hold the first crossings open and to keep the groves from breaking into the growing kingdoms.

rites.name: Rasostanum
rites.text: A tuned talent that a weapon can carry, shaping how its wielder fights. It belongs to the family of talents that modify armaments.

rites.name: Vantornor
rites.text: A set of specialized abilities that a person can pick up to change how they operate. Each ability grants combat advantages that shape how engagements turn out, whether they lean toward attack or support.

rites.name: Sianaurium
rites.text: A talent that lets a wielder's weapons be enhanced by a magnetic force, granting them a boost in power. It belongs to the set of abilities tied to armaments.

rites.name: Veontus
rites.text: A special talent that alters the ammunition fired from a weapon. It belongs to the class of combat techniques that a user can attach to firearms.

rites.name: Sereleostor
rites.text: A talent tied to weapons that the text names briefly and gives no further detail on. It belongs to a set of combat abilities that shape how armed fighters operate.

rites.name: Saurnia
rites.text: A core strength measure that raises the striking power of every armed weapon a bearer carries. It also unlocks special combat skills once a minimum level is reached, and it links to a guardian hall within the bearer's stronghold.

rites.name: Tosines
rites.text: A recognized deed a fighter performs in battle, marked by its own sigil and rewarded with extra progress once the clash ends. Certain worn guards can multiply these rewards.

rites.name: Oriallesor
rites.text: A bold trait that can be carried by a wide range of handheld projectile arms, from pocket pistols to heavy shotguns and long-range marksman rifles.

rites.name: Niria
rites.text: A tactical skill that lets a fighter strike along several lines at once, and an enhanced form of it that sharpens the same technique.

rites.name: Ternus
rites.text: A modern battlefield knack that lets a weapon keep sounding out a steady stream of noise. It belongs to the set of talents a gun can carry.

rites.name: Maullum
rites.text: A learned talent that lets a fighter's weapon handling sharpen and adjust to the moment. It belongs to the set of combat gifts a warrior can cultivate.

rites.name: Caulum
rites.text: A tactical skill that lets a wielder of armed gear confuse pursuers and draw aim away from themselves. A sharpened version of this skill grants a stronger version of the same effect.

rites.name: Meorelus
rites.text: A combat gift that lets a hunter's weapon strike harder against towering foes. It is one of the talents a fighter can attach to their arms.

rites.name: Tistum
rites.text: A learned knack that lets a wielder handle armaments with swift, nimble motions. It belongs to the broader craft of combat skills kept by the modern settlers.

rites.name: Cosiares
rites.text: A fighter who fires while sheltered gains a growing edge in striking power for a short span. Felling a foe while sheltered renews that span, but reloading, changing arms, or leaving the fight ends the advantage at once.

rites.name: Sellostia
rites.text: A discipline for long-barrel shooters that rewards landing precise strikes to the head. Each sustained run of such hits unlocks three boons: harder blows, extra protection, and quicker reloads.

rites.name: Celum
rites.text: A learned knack that lets a fighter with a particular arm draw strength from the arm's own gear. It is one of several skills honed by warriors of the age.

rites.name: Marnanum
rites.text: A bearer's weapon gift that sharpens a fighter's combat skill when wielded. A stronger, refined version of the same gift also exists.

rites.name: Tisiaranum
rites.text: A deadly skill tied to weapons, granting a fighter a lethal edge in combat. A stronger, refined form of it also exists, sharpening the same deadly craft.

rites.name: Niantor
rites.text: A marksman's rifle talent that lodges its round inside the struck foe and detonates it a moment later. The blast deals bonus harm scaled to the shooter's firearm strength.

rites.name: Valialanum
rites.text: A combat gift that lets a wielder of a firearm draw strength from their weapon's handling. It is a talent tied to the skill of arms.

rites.name: Telines
rites.text: A combat technique in which a fighter strikes a foe's weakest seams to shatter their guard. An improved form exists that deepens the blow.

rites.name: Nolaunus
rites.text: A traveler marks a known waypoint, presses a chosen key, and is instantly carried there. Companions can watch the traveler's glowing path across the map.

rites.name: Sialleres
rites.text: A stored-charge talent that lets a wielder's arms draw on a spare energy reserve. A stronger variant of this talent exists for those who unlock it.

rites.name: Nirnus
rites.text: A tactical knack that lets a wielder of a firearm unleash a dense torrent of shots that saturates an area. It is a talent that rewards those who favor sustained, overwhelming fire.

rites.name: Niasauror
rites.text: A combat gift that lets a wielder draw strength from wounds they have already taken. An enhanced form of this gift grants even greater power to those who fight through their own injuries.

rites.name: Cirestor
rites.text: A tactical gift tied to a field weapon, granting its wielder a special talent in a modern conflict setting. It is a bonus that shapes how a weapon performs in combat.

rites.name: Sastanum
rites.text: A talent that lets a wielder of firearms bring an enemy's offensive to an abrupt halt. It belongs to the arsenal of weapon-craft in a modern war-torn city.

rites.name: Nauntalium
rites.text: A battle skill tied to the handling of arms, granted to those who wield weapons in a fractured modern city. It reshapes how a fighter uses their gear.

rites.name: Mirnanum
rites.text: A tactical knack that lets a wielder of a firearm replenish its rounds more quickly. A stronger version of this knack exists and makes the effect greater.

rites.name: Sinerium
rites.text: A set of boons that take hold only while a wanderer walks within a contested hollow. Each boon grants a survival advantage, one chosen per rank, and the rank rises and falls with the wanderer's deeds inside the hollow.

rites.name: Liasentes
rites.text: A trained composure gift that lets a wielder of a firearm keep steady aim under pressure. An improved form of the same gift sharpens that steadiness further.

rites.name: Orilianum
rites.text: A combat gift that lets a fighter grow sharper and more dangerous with each foe felled. A stronger version of the same gift exists, enhancing this power further.

rites.name: Oraunia
rites.text: A combat talent tied to weaponry that marks a fighter's opening strike. It belongs to the arsenal of skills a wielder can draw upon in battle.

rites.name: Tasor
rites.text: A tiered system of three branches lets a wanderer shape their own calling. Active gifts recharge after use and swap freely, triggered gifts fire under set conditions, and constant gifts stack together to amplify one another.

rites.name: Amaullanium
rites.text: A talent that empowers a weapon, granting its wielder a special ability when used in combat. It belongs to the modern arsenal of the setting's survivors.

rites.name: Viantistes
rites.text: A hidden talent that lets a weapon strike unseen, granted to a few firearms of security and tactical forces. It belongs to the armaments used by police and special units.

rites.name: Ceontarum
rites.text: A healer's bond of trust, held between a physician and those she treats. It requires helping whoever suffers, regardless of which side they serve.

rites.name: Tiarnor
rites.text: A core attribute that strengthens an agent's special abilities, with each point granting thirty units of skill power. It is raised by equipping gear tuned to it and gates certain weapon talents that manage ability use and cooldowns.

rites.name: Telolus
rites.text: A learned knack that lets a fighter handle several tasks at the same time while wielding weapons. A stronger refined form of the same knack exists.

rites.name: Caurnes
rites.text: A knack that lets a wielder's weapon strike with fortune at unexpected moments. It is a talent tied to firearms, granting an occasional chance of an especially fortunate shot.

rites.name: Ceorniantus
rites.text: A quiet knack for careful handling that lets a user bring out steadier results from certain handheld firearms of several types. It suits those who favor precision over speed.

rites.name: Amastolum
rites.text: A combat talent tied to weapons that lets a wielder bring foes to yield. It belongs to the arms-craft of a modern, technology-driven age.

rites.name: Tiarnintes
rites.text: A returning throwing-arc skill that lets a wielder hurl a curved implement which arcs back to them. It is taught as a talent within a combat tradition of weapon arts.

rites.name: Tellum
rites.text: A combat skill that rewards a fighter for staying in close quarters with a weapon. It is one of the talents a warrior can develop within a larger conflict.

rites.name: Castaunus
rites.text: A battlefield skill that sharpens the aim of those who tend the wounded. An improved form of this talent refines that precision further.

rites.name: Miastasum
rites.text: A held technique that lets a wielder steady a handheld armament and guide its discharge with greater command. It can be applied to a range of small firing implements, from pistols to rifles and scatter-blasters.

rites.name: Neostium
rites.text: A set of forty permanent passive gifts that a wanderer gains once each is awakened. Once claimed, every gift stays active at all times and need not be chosen or switched.

rites.name: Melia Coronilus
rites.text: A talent that lets a wielder's weapon hold a full store of energy, releasing it in a single strong burst. An enhanced version of the same craft exists.

rites.name: Tilestanum
rites.text: A combat skill that lets a fighter adjust their methods to the weapon in hand. An improved form of the same skill refines this adjustment further.

rites.name: Ceriastus
rites.text: A shared bond of fighters that grows stronger as companions take down marked foes. Each ally's effort adds to the wielder's power in combat.

rites.name: Seornor
rites.text: A held craft that lets a fighter draw on a secondary defensive reserve during battle. An enhanced form of the same reserve strengthens the practice further.

rites.name: Siareostor
rites.text: A practiced knack that lets a fighter carry and restock projectile supplies more effectively. A stronger, refined form of the same knack grants even greater reserves.

rites.name: Corantum
rites.text: A specialized combat skill that empowers a fighter's weapon handling. An enhanced version of the same technique refines its power.

rites.name: Meosintor
rites.text: A combat technique that lets a fighter focus gunfire into one narrow point of attack. A strengthened form of the technique pushes that focus even further.

rites.name: Tastellia
rites.text: A talent that lets a weapon inflict lingering pain on its target. It belongs to the set of special abilities that arms can carry.

rites.name: Serellum
rites.text: A practiced skill that lets a fighter tag distant foes so allies can aim at them more easily. A stronger, refined form of the technique reinforces the same mark.

rites.name: Kelarunar
rites.text: kelarunar is a clandestine ritual performed by the nomadic tribe of the Verdant Veil on the night of the equinox, during which they channel the collective will of the forest into a single luminous orb that can heal any wound or cure any disease. the orb, known as the Luminous Heart, is created by binding the life force of a thousand saplings with the echo of a dying star. when released, it emits a pulse that restores health to all living beings within a radius of several kilometers, but at the cost of draining the surrounding flora of their vitality.

rites.name: Kelurock
rites.text: Nexus, an omnipresent AI in the Chronoverse, facilitates temporal communication, event analysis, and holographic archiving, serving as a temporal guide for Timekeepers.

rites.name: Kelernolden
rites.text: Kelernolden is a catch-all name for a suite of field-gear used by a grounded covert service, spanning launch pods, deployable shields, seeker charges, portable relay stations, lens overlays, and wrist-worn devices all tied to a shared sensor mesh. It exists to give small teams a coordinated edge without any single device being decisive on its own.

rites.name: Thostuldock
rites.text: Thostuldock is a grounded, six-age-old doctrine of field tools that Crodaston's relief corps uses to stabilize crises: a kit of medical, engineering, and defensive devices drawn from three disciplines. Each device can be fired once, then must cool for a fixed interval before it answers again, and crews may bind two standing devices and one signature rig at a time.

rites.name: Keledar
rites.text: Keledar is a grounded scanning discipline in the Crodaston of the fourth age, practiced by wardens who read the faint heat and electrical hum of hidden people through stone and cover. Its practitioners project the findings onto a thin lattice of light before their eyes, and some claim the lattice occasionally reveals forgotten caches as well. The technique has splintered into five schools, each with its own name and purpose.

rites.name: Fenuldedar
rites.text: Fenuldedar is a squat, tripod-legged sentry platform that Crodaston's lowland militias deploy to guard supply depots and mountain passes. It holds its ground on its own judgment or obeys a handler's hand on a wired trigger, and its shielded housing lets it survive a long siege of crossfire.

rites.name: Jorasteld
rites.text: Jorasteld is a rolling sphere of humming brass that trundles across broken ground toward whatever its keepers mark for it, ending its journey in a sharp, contained burst. Scavenger crews in Crodaston's lower districts count on its small, honest fury more than any rifle.

rites.name: Kelordar
rites.text: Kelordar is a collapsible barrier of layered ceramic-polymer plating that unfolds from a wrist housing in under a second, locking into a broad panel that stops projectiles from the front while its bearer stays exposed behind it. Field engineers of the Vantreth Compact carry it into breaches where cover is scarce, and its hardened edges can also be braced to shove a crowd back.

rites.name: Halornade
rites.text: The Luminex Disperser is a rail‑mounted emitter that releases charged aerosol clouds across a battlefield.  Each cloud carries a distinct field—repair, ignition, immobilization, or corrosive—allowing a single device to support, disrupt, or damage enemies from a safe distance.  Its modular cartridges can be swapped in seconds, turning the Disperser into a versatile tool for both offense and defense.

rites.name: Morurdanen
rites.text: Morurdanen is a hovering support drone built by the Crodaston Grounded engineers, designed to be tasked with a single target and shadow it through the chaos of a street fight. Its signature is a tethered signal lattice that lets it flag enemies for allies and patch damaged plating mid-fire. It is cheap enough to deploy by the dozen and fragile enough that losing one is an accepted cost.

rites.name: Moraron
rites.text: Moraron is a small, hovering drone-like construct from the Crodaston concept line, built to hunt down a marked target and deliver a single tailored payload. Its variants specialize in blinding, bursting, and demolishing, each tuned to a different battlefield problem.

rites.name: Brurde
rites.text: Brurde is a ground-thrown swarm device in the Crodaston grounded realm, scattering clouds of tiny hovering engines that can mend, sting, revive, or empower those nearby. Its many attuned forms are sold in the lower markets of Erevald Quarter as tools for field medics and reckless duelists alike. Because it is cheap and easy to deploy, it has become a staple of the region's informal militias.

rites.name: Crestorde
rites.text: Crestorde is a tacky, sticky charge worn as a grudge-bomb by street mechanics in the Crodaston underworld. Once fixed to a surface or a target, it waits for a handheld pulse before going off with a gritty bang.

rites.name: Drernade
rites.text: Drernade is a hand-thrown canister in the Crodaston grounded age, prized by scavenger crews for scattering a loose field of tiny proximity-triggered charges across any ground it lands on. Each salvaged canister carries a sealed tuning key that alters which kind of charge the field produces, and no two crews have ever agreed on how the keys were cut.

rites.name: Dreneld
rites.text: Dreneld is a palm-sized lattice of mirrored glass that its user tosses into a firefight, where it blooms into a still, shimmering double of its bearer for a short while. Hostile gunners fixate on the false figure, buying the real agent time to slip away, and in the lawless Dark Zone the decoy also wears the agent's stolen nameplate.

rites.name: Halere
rites.text: Halere is a field discipline in Crodaston's Grounded realm, practiced by wardens who raise shelter from the air itself. Its adepts can fling a tethered bulwark that clings to anyone standing close, hardening their defenses or sharpening their strikes.

rites.name: Fenedar
rites.text: Fenedar is a field medic's craft of the Crodaston Grounded realm, passed through the sixth age of the Orrin Collegia as a set of practiced disciplines. Its practitioners lay hands and tend wounds, plant portable restoratives, and, in their rarest art, call a pulse of living warmth that rouses every comrade nearby from the edge of death.

rites.name: Brunerdon
rites.text: Brunerdon is a battlefield discipline in Crodaston's sixth era, in which a trained combatant tunes their own weapon's resonance so that strikes hit harder and blades hold their edge longer for everyone fighting within reach. It is one of three foundational Signature Skills taught to the grounded soldiers of the age.

rites.name: Haludock
rites.text: Haludock is a resonant chant-stance taught in the river monasteries of Crodaston, where practitioners hum in shared pitch so the whole circle steadies its bodies against blows and hastens its footwork. When a wielder would otherwise fall to a fatal wound, the chant turns inward and forces a surge of restorative breath through the damaged tissue.

rites.name: Morunernath
rites.text: Morunernath is a Crodaston discipline of signature techniques, each bound to a dedicated gesture and carried in a reserved slot that ignores ordinary training modifiers. Once any member of a circle invokes a given technique, that technique falls silent for the whole circle for a full minute, forcing the group to rotate its strongest tools.

rites.name: Cresturde
rites.text: Cresturde is a grounded concept, a set of six disciplines that a Crodaston field operative can commit to after years of service. Each discipline shapes its adherents' gear, favored tools, and combat style, turning the operative into a specialist. The system is less about raw power than about how a person chooses to be useful when the city falls apart.

rites.name: Halardeldar
rites.text: Halardeldar is a combat creed of the ironbound clans, centered on entangling snares and volatile projectiles. its warriors fire the thunder‑spike bow, plant self‑healing pulse mines, and hurl flame‑burst canisters to dominate any fight. the doctrine thrives in the lowlands of Crodaston, where every step can become a trap and every wound a chance to ignite.

rites.name: Moraduren
rites.text: Moraduren is a grounded combat discipline in Crodaston's sixth era, built around the belief that a battlefield is shaped by where a person refuses to let others stand. Its practitioners carry a repeating multi-shot launcher loaded with fragmenting bombs and learn to lay down overlapping kill-zones that bleed opponents slowly and force them into retreat. Practitioners are valued for denying ground rather than seizing it.

rites.name: Thardorath
rites.text: Thardorath is a long-range marksman doctrine practiced in the high ridges of Crodaston's southern reach, where wardens rely on patient precision over brute force. Its adherents carry heavy bolt-action rifles, reconnaissance drones tuned for scouting, and blinding thunder-charges to break enemy formations before the shot is taken.

rites.name: Tarnodeld
rites.text: Tarnodeld is a heavy weapons specialist who wields a rotary cannon that chews through walls and a spray that hardens on contact to trap enemies. The gunner can pin down a whole squad while anchored behind a crumbling barricade.

rites.name: Pelardon
rites.text: Pelardon is a field engineer of the Crodaston wastes who keeps the scavenged machines of the old towns running and hot-wires them into the fight. Carrying a rattling rocket rig, a hive of salvaged augmentation drones, and a satchel of pulse charges, Pelardon turns mechanical chaos into a tactical advantage. Their talent is most valued where a single machine failure can doom a whole crew.

rites.name: Tarnalde
rites.text: Tarnalde is a close-quarters combat discipline in Crodaston's sixth era, favored by breach teams who fight in collapsed corridors and shattered streets. Its practitioners pair a compact jet-fed flame projector with a shield that doubles as a fire-shaping plate, and they carry clustered charges to clear rooms ahead of their advance. The discipline values steady nerve and coordinated pressure over raw force.

rites.name: Crostenock
rites.text: Crostenock is a concept of disciplined field talents, quiet reflexes earned through practice rather than raw power, that activate when a combatant meets a precise condition in the middle of a fight. Its wings each hold a set of talents, and a bearer may keep four in play at once, so the skill lies in choosing which four a moment demands.

rites.name: Moreldunar
rites.text: Moreldunar is a sealed chime of the Crodaston Accord, struck once per healing ritual so that restored vigor spills past its usual limits as a brief shimmering surplus. Its binding lapses within a few hours, leaving the recipient no stronger than before once the glow fades.

rites.name: Tharnen
rites.text: Tharnen is a mending ritual in the grounded era of Crodaston, where a person who tends their wounds with salve and bandage gains a hardened tolerance to later harm. Its practitioners say the deeper the wound, the more steadily the body learns to hold against the next blow.

rites.name: Jorarden
rites.text: Jorarden is a sealed binding-art in the Grounded realm of Crodaston, practiced in the sixth age by wardens who bind unruly spirits into hollow glass. When a warden seals a hostile, the binding briefly lends the warden a rush of quickened stride.

rites.name: Halaron
rites.text: Halaron is a tide-bound discipline in Crodaston's grounded era, practiced by wayfarers who measure their strength by how far they carry a single rhythm across open country. Each unbroken stride across a landscape gathers force into the blade they carry, and the practice is taught in the silt-flats where long journeys begin.

rites.name: Thene
rites.text: Thene is a drifting technique in the Crodaston powers tradition, taught in the grounded era of the sixth age as a way for couriers to slip between shelters under fire. The practitioner's body bends the force of incoming strikes into a brief, shimmering wake that scatters most of their weight before it lands.

rites.name: Kelardeston
rites.text: Kelardeston is a stabilizing discipline taught in the frontier garrisons of Crodaston, where soldiers learn to brace their bodies against the kick of their arms. Practitioners who take shelter behind a barrier momentarily steady their grip and aim, letting the weapon's backward thrust bleed away into the ground.

rites.name: Keladath
rites.text: Keladath is a grounded concept in the Crodaston omniverse, a ritual of focused sight where a wielder's gaze tags a target with a faint luminous sigil. The sigil briefly outlines the marked figure through walls and debris, guiding allies to hidden positions.

rites.name: Crodeld
rites.text: Crodeld is the quiet accumulation of hard-won habits that a settlement's people carry with them, each one a standing advantage that never needs to be called upon or equipped. Once a habit has been earned through the upkeep of a home base, it operates continuously alongside every other habit the people have gathered. Its reach is modest, measured in the ordinary strength of a laborer or the steadiness of a field medic.

rites.name: Draldornon
rites.text: Draldornon is a catch-all name for a grounded suite of field gear used by a small civic response corps in the sixth era of Crodaston, bundling deployable pods, collapsible barriers, mines, and wearable displays into one networked kit. Its equipment is tuned for practical, bounded tasks, and the whole network is meant to keep responders coordinated under pressure rather than to overpower the threats they face.

rites.name: Theldore
rites.text: Theldore is a continent-spanning relay lattice of orbital mirrors and buried signal vaults, threaded through the minds of its keepers and answered from a central vault beneath the capital. Its reach fails wherever the air has been scorched by old anomalies, leaving keepers to speak only by voice and hand until the lattice relearns the place.

rites.name: Morunedock
rites.text: Morunedock is a grounded, non-combat analysis suite woven into the transceivers of Crodaston's field agents, quietly tracking heat signatures, gait, and the faint residues left by passing crowds. Its signature trick is replaying the last few minutes of a location as a shimmering reconstruction that agents can walk through and question. It is a tool of memory and inference rather than force, and its most dramatic act is outlasting the rooms it reconstructs.

rites.name: Keleren
rites.text: Keleren is a self-organizing lattice pattern that awakens in deep mineral veins, releasing stored strain as coherent light. Survey teams track its pulse to locate hidden cavities, though the glow can fracture rock if left unchecked.

rites.name: Moraldedath
rites.text: Moraldedath is a non-conversational tactical intelligence woven through the Crodaston operative grid, coordinating field teams through silent, precise relays of routing data and threat assessments. Built for a grounded era where information outweighs spectacle, it has never spoken a word to the people it guides, only issuing the cues that keep them alive.

rites.name: Brarnuldon
rites.text: Brarnuldon is a grounded concept: a training-grade reasoning engine built into a city's emergency response network, designed to rehearse disaster drills from sensor feeds. It can reconstruct any scene its operators record into a rehearsal space, a quiet capability that later drew a rival faction seeking to copy recorded subjects into the physical world.

rites.name: Moranerdock
rites.text: Moranerdock is a concept-class fixture of Crodaston's grounded Sixth Era, a lattice of humming reliquary lenses that reassemble the echoes of a town's daily noise into shimmering reconstructions of what once occurred there. Residents trust its reconstructions more than their own memories, and the lattice is consulted whenever a household loses track of someone.

rites.name: Kelustar
rites.text: Kelustar is a grounded war-machine concept in the E6 era, a four-year-old design lineage built around a hovering field-support frame. Its variants are meant to keep soldiers alive, mark targets, and deliver small but deadly payloads from above. Each variant is tuned to a narrow combat role rather than general destruction.
